questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that rectifies the underlined group of words in the given sentence. Despite having been stripped of all official administrative powers during the initial corporate purge, the founder continued to influence executive decisions from behind the scenes.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that rectifies the underlined group of words in the given sentence.

Despite having been stripped of all official administrative powers during the initial corporate purge, the founder continued to influence executive decisions from behind the scenes.

options.text: Although stripped of all official administrative powers
options.html: Although stripped of all official administrative powers

options.text: Despite being stripped from all official administrative powers
options.html: Despite being stripped from all official administrative powers

options.text: Inspite of having stripped of all official administrative powers
options.html: Inspite of having stripped of all official administrative powers

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. No improvement needed .

Key Points

  • The sentence is already correct and uses the appropriate structure and phrasing.
  • The phrase "Despite having been stripped of all official administrative powers" is grammatically correct and effectively conveys the intended meaning.
  • It correctly uses "Despite" to indicate contrast and "having been stripped" to show the action completed in the past.

Correct sentence: Despite having been stripped of all official administrative powers during the initial corporate purge, the founder continued to influence executive decisions from behind the scenes.

Additional Information

  • Alternative Options Analysis:
    • Option 1: "Although stripped of all official administrative powers" – While grammatically correct, it changes the original structure unnecessarily.
    • Option 2: "Despite being stripped from all official administrative powers" – Incorrect usage of "stripped from" instead of "stripped of."
    • Option 3: "Inspite of having stripped of all official administrative powers" – Incorrect spelling of "Inspite" (should be "In spite") and awkward phrasing.

questions.question: In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select “No improvement”. She is taller than any other girls in the group.
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select “No improvement”.

She is taller than any other girls in the group.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: any other girl

Key Points

  • The given sentence says that she is taller than any other girls in the group. If she is taller than all the girls then she is the tallest girl in the group.
  • Taller is the comparative degree for tall. A comparative degree is used to comparative two separate persons or things or groups.
  • When we use a comparative degree + than with the expression 'any other', the noun that follows should be singular.
  • So, the structure becomes: comparative degree + than + any other + singular noun
  • But, in the given sentence, any other is followed by girls which is a plural noun. It does not satisfy the rule. So, Option 4 gets ruled out.
  • Every other should always be followed by a singular noun but in Option 1 it is followed by girls which is plural. So, Option 1 gets ruled out.
  • Each other is never followed by a noun but in Option 2 it is followed by girl which is a noun. So, Option 2 also gets ruled out.
  • Any other girl is the appropriate entry here because it satisfies the above-mentioned rule. Hence, Option 3 is the correct answer.

Thus, the correct answer is: She is taller than any other girl in the group.

Additional Information

  • When we interchange degrees of comparison, we follow the following rules.
  • Let's take a sentence for an instance. For example- He was the fastest boy in the race.
  • The given sentence says that he was faster than all other boys in the race.
  • So, when we change superlative degree into comparative degree, we follow the following structures.
  • comparative degree + than + any other + singular noun
    • ​Example- He was faster than any other boy in the race.
  • ​comparative degree + than + all other + plural noun
    • ​Example- He was faster than all other boys in the race.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to improve the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to improve it, select ‘No improvement required. I hate my mother, sister and almost all the women. I am a misogamist.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to improve the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to improve it, select ‘No improvement required.

I hate my mother, sister and almost all the women. I am a misogamist.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "misogynist"
Key Points
  • "misogynist" will replace "misogamist"
  • A person who hates women is known as a misogynist.
  • This sentence is talking about hatred towards women so misogynist is the best option.
  • Look at the examples:
    • She if a girl but she is misogynist.
Hence, the correct sentence is: I hate my mother, sister, and almost all the women. I am a misogynist.
Hinglish
  • यहां पर misogamist की जगह misogynist आएगा
  • जो शादी से नफरत करता है उसको misgamist बोलते हैं
  • इस sentence में औरतों से नफरत के बारे में बात हो रही है
  • औरतों से नफरत करने वालों को misogynist बोलते हैं

Additional Information

  • let's look at the other words
    • misogamist- one who hates marriage
    • Philogynist- one who loves women
    • Polygynist- one who marries many women.
    • psychologist- one who treats mental disease

questions.question: Direction: Select the most appropriate option to improve the underlined segment in the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement'. Film industry is facing the challenge of television screen which, because of its ready availability and nearness to entertainment seekers, is becoming very popular.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Select the most appropriate option to improve the underlined segment in the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement'.

Film industry is facing the challenge of television screen which, because of its ready availability and nearness to entertainment seekers, is becoming very popular.

options.text: The film industry is facing the challenge of the
options.html: The film industry is facing the challenge of the

options.text: Film industry is facing a challenge of a
options.html: Film industry is facing a challenge of a

options.text: Film industry is facing challenge of
options.html: Film industry is facing challenge of

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'The film industry is facing the challenge of the.'

Key Points

  • The only articles in English are ‘the’ and ‘a/an’.
  • Use the article "a or an" to indicate any non-specified member of a group or category.
  • If a word begins with a vowel sound, then the correct article is 'an'; otherwise, if it begins with a consonantal sound, the correct article is 'a'.
  • The definite article 'the' is used before a noun to indicate that the identity of the noun is known to the reader. 
    • Example: 
      • We are looking for an apartment.
      • I own a cat and two dogs.
      • I love to visit the building.
  • Here, we are talking about the specific 'film industry', 'challenge', and 'television', therefore 'the' must be used before them.
  • Thus, the correct answer is Option 1.
     

​Correct sentence: The film industry is facing the challenge of the television screen which, because of its ready availability and nearness to entertainment seekers, is becoming very popular.

questions.question: Select the word that needs to be changed to make the sentence correct. Select "No correction required" if there is no need for correction. The dog jumped in the hurdle.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the word that needs to be changed to make the sentence correct. Select "No correction required" if there is no need for correction.

The dog jumped in the hurdle.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4.
 
Key Points
  • The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect preposition "in" used before the term "the hurdle."
  • The correct preposition for this context is "over".
  • The correct phrase should be "over the hurdle," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.
 
Correct Sentence: "The dog jumped over the hurdle."

questions.question: In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement'. Not drinking has certain made a real difference to him.
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement'.

Not drinking has certain made a real difference to him.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is- 'has certainly made'.

Key Points

  • Modifiers: Modifiers are usually placed next to the word they modify. Adjectives as modifiers come more often before the noun than after it. Adverbs as modifiers occur immediately before or after the verb, and before an adjective or another adverb.
  • Adverb as modifiers: Adverb modifies a verb, adjective, and adverb.
    • Adverb modifying verb: She breathes heavily. (The adverb 'heavily' modifies the verb 'breathes')
    • Adverb modifying an adjective: He is really funny.  (The adverb 'really' modifies the adjective 'funny')
    • Adverb modifying an adverb: We whisper very softly to each other. (The adverb 'very' modifies the adverb 'softly') 
  • In the given sentence 'certain' is an adjective and an adjective does not modify a verb 'made'. 
  • Therefore 'certain' should be replaced by 'certainly'. This is because 'certainly' is an adverb and it modifies the verb 'made'.
  • Hence, option 2 is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: Not drinking has certainly made a real difference to him.

Important Points

  • Most adverbs end in -ly. Only a few words ending in -ly are adjective.
  • Example: Real is an adjective; really is an adverb.
  • Example: The company is aware of the really problems that these people face.
  • The above example is incorrect because an adverb does not modify a noun. The word 'really' is an adverb.

questions.question: Direction: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The Siachen Glacier is the northern point on the LOC.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The Siachen Glacier is the northern point on the LOC.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'northernmost.'

Key Points

  • We use a superlative to say that a thing or person is the most of a group.
  • When we use a superlative adjective ('the tallest student') before the noun, we generally use it with 'the'.  
  • In this case, we will add –most to the end of the two-syllable word to make a superlative degree.
  • So, 'northernmost' is the superlative degree of the adjective and is appropriate for the given blank as the sentence is talking about the most northern point on the LOC.
  • Hence, option 1 is the correct answer. 
    ​

​Correct sentence: The Siachen Glacier is the northernmost point on the LOC.

The family is neither interested in selling the property or rebuilding it.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that rectifies the underlined group of words in the given sentence. The regulatory agency insisted that the laboratory adhere to the environmental parameters, but the management flatly refused to comply with.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that rectifies the underlined group of words in the given sentence.

The regulatory agency insisted that the laboratory adhere to the environmental parameters, but the management flatly refused to comply with.

options.text: flatly refused to comply with them
options.html: flatly refused to comply with them

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. flatly refused to comply .

Key Points

  • The sentence provided is grammatically incorrect because the phrase "refused to comply with" is incomplete without specifying what the compliance is directed towards (e.g., "comply with them").
  • However, the most appropriate correction eliminates redundancy, as the context already makes it clear that the laboratory refused compliance. Thus, the phrase "refused to comply" is concise and sufficient.
  • Option 1, "flatly refused to comply with them," is unnecessarily wordy and introduces ambiguity regarding the antecedent of "them."
  • Option 3, "flatly refused compliance to," is grammatically incorrect because "compliance" is not followed by "to" but by "with."
  • Option 4, "No improvement needed," is incorrect because the original sentence is incomplete and awkward.

Correct sentence: The regulatory agency insisted that the laboratory adhere to the environmental parameters, but the management flatly refused to comply.

Additional Information

  • Usage of "comply":
    • "Comply" is always followed by "with," not "to" or "for."
    • Example: The staff complied with the new rules.
  • Redundancy: Avoid adding unnecessary words when the meaning is already clear. In this case, "comply" alone conveys the intended meaning.
